It depends on which contrast measure you count as "WCAG AA".

| Measure | Ratio | AA body text (4.5) |
|---|---|---|
| Classic WCAG 2.x luminance ratio (`--type wcag2`) | **5.6** | Pass |
| OKCA in klar, #0055ff text on #ffffff | **4.3** | Fail |

- **Formal compliance:** the letter of WCAG 2.x is the classic formula, so #0055ff on white passes AA at 5.6. That is the number a WCAG audit or an automated checker like axe or Lighthouse will report.
- **Perceptual view:** OKCA is the project's default in klar. It is polarity-aware, so dark text on white scores lower, and it puts this pair at 4.3, below 4.5. If your team gates on klar or wants a perceptual margin, this color doesn't clear it.

Which to trust depends on what you're held to:
- **Formal WCAG 2.x conformance:** use it.
- **Klar's OKCA as the bar:** don't use it for body text. It would be fine for large text (3.0 threshold) either way.
